Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborating GSMA-sourced (DataReportal) data show mobile connections at 54.7% of population (2023) rising to 59.4% (Jan 2024); ITU-sourced subscriptions data (TheGlobalEconomy) show 65.74 subscriptions per 100 people (2023). All of these are connections/subscriptions rather than unique-subscriber counts, so they likely overstate true unique-subscriber penetration (Niger has a lower connectivity-enabler score than the Sub-Saharan average). No primary GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber percentage could be retrieved (dynamic/paywalled). Code 3 (40-54%) remains a reasonable, corroborated estimate, but the exact figure is close to the 3/4 boundary — recommend human review against a primary GSMA unique-subscriber figure if available.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the primary legal texts (Loi n°2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection, amended by Loi n°2023-31 of 2023) and DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World. Niger's HAPDP (Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) is an independent administrative authority attached to the Presidency, with legal personality, financial autonomy, and powers to sanction non-compliant data controllers — this substantiates code 4 (legislation enacted with DPA established). No verified evidence of actual enforcement decisions/fines was found, so an upgrade to code 5 (mature framework with active enforcement) is not supported.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Updated RISE (World Bank/ESMAP) data shows a current, officially approved electrification plan (governance sub-score 82/100) with a dedicated mini-grids framework (65/100) covering solar hybrid mini-grid programmes and diesel-to-solar hybridisation. The World Bank's Niger Solar Electricity Access Project (NESAP), closed December 2024, delivered new solar mini-grid connections to c.1,464 households and hybridised existing NIGELEC mini-grids for c.19,283 households, evidencing continued but partial deployment; overall national electricity access remains very low (20%, World Bank 2023). This confirms code 3 (active policy with some deployment) on fresher (2023-2024) sources than the original 2019 citation; it is a borderline case that could approach code 4 in future but current deployment scale does not yet meet 'significant deployment' at national level.
